info.title: Assetbots API 1.0
info.description: Use the Assetbots API to sync your Assetbots database with other software and apps used by your organization.

get.summary: Gets all of the assets in the database.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of assets to get, from 1 to 1,000.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The offset to start fetching at.

parameters.name: $filter
parameters.description:
Optionally filter the results based on one or more field keys. Uses OData-like syntax e.g., "serialNumber eq 1234 and brand eq Apple" (without quotes). Must be escaped properly for use in a query string.
Supported comparison operators include: eq (equal), gt (greater-than), ge (greater-than-or-equal), lt (less-than), le (less-than-or-equal), nq (not-equal).
Supported logical operators include: and, or.

tags.name: Assets
tags.description:
Assets are anything valuable you want to keep track of. Assetbots help you
track their location, lifespan, depreciation and more.

tags.name: CheckIns
tags.description: Check-ins unassign assets from people, locations or both.

tags.name: Checkouts
tags.description: Checkouts assign assets to people, locations or both.

tags.name: Databases
tags.description: Databases contain all of your asset data and settings.

tags.name: Locations
tags.description: Locations are places, physical or otherwise, where assets can be assigned.

tags.name: Notes
tags.description:
Notes are a way to record important details or observations.
Use notes to document updates, insights, or reminders related to assets and people.

tags.name: People
tags.description: The People directory allows you to keep track of who has custody of assets.

tags.name: RepairCompletions
tags.description: Repair completion is responsible for initiating, completing, or canceling repair operations.

tags.name: Repairs
tags.description: Repairs extend asset lifetimes through routine and restorative maintenance.
